topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-119, when a licensee advertises or promotes his real estate activities, the advertisement must include:
choice_a: The licensee's personal cell phone number only
choice_b: The MLS listing number only
choice_c: The licensee's continuing education hours
choice_d: The real estate company name under which the licensee is licensed by the commission
explanation: W.S. 33-28-119(a), (f) and (g) require every licensee, when advertising real estate activity, to use the real estate company name under which he is licensed. None of the other items is a statutory advertising requirement.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A responsible broker wants to promote his business under a trade name different from his licensed company name. Under W.S. 33-28-119(e), this is permitted only if:
choice_a: The trade name owner consents and the licensed real estate company name is still displayed conspicuously as prescribed by commission rules
choice_b: The commission first issues a separate license for the trade name
choice_c: It is never permitted under Wyoming law
choice_d: The trade name is used only at branch offices, never the principal office
explanation: Under 33-28-119(e), a trade name may be used concurrently with the licensed company name only with the trade-name owner's permission, and the licensed company name must still be displayed conspicuously so the public can identify it. There is no separate trade-name license.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A salesperson lists and advertises her own personally owned home for sale. Under W.S. 33-28-119(h), the advertisement must:
choice_a: Omit her name entirely to avoid a conflict of interest
choice_b: Disclose the fact that an owner of the real estate is a licensee
choice_c: Be approved in advance by the commission
choice_d: Use only the company logo, with no personal identification
explanation: W.S. 33-28-119(h) requires that when a licensee advertises real estate he owns, the advertisement disclose that an owner of the property is a licensee. Nothing in the statute requires prior commission approval or bars use of her name.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A licensee whose legal first name is "Willard" wants his advertisements to use the nickname "Skip." Under W.S. 33-28-119(j), this is permitted only if:
choice_a: The nickname has been used by the licensee for at least one year
choice_b: His responsible broker approves the nickname in writing
choice_c: The nickname is reflected on the licensee's license
choice_d: The commission issues a waiver
explanation: Under 33-28-119(j), a licensee's advertisement must include the first and last name, though a common shortened spelling of the first name is allowed; a nickname is permitted only if it is reflected on the license itself.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Which of the following is expressly identified in W.S. 33-28-111(a)(vi) as grounds for discipline?
choice_a: Advertising a listing on a weekend
choice_b: Placing a yard sign with the owner's written consent
choice_c: Advertising using the licensee's own registered service mark
choice_d: Using advertising that is misleading or inaccurate in any matter material to the transaction
explanation: 33-28-111(a)(vi) makes it grounds for discipline to use advertising that is misleading or inaccurate on a matter material to the transaction, or that uses another's trade name, mark or logo without authorization. Advertising with owner consent or one's own mark is not a violation.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A Wyoming salesperson wants to change her contractual affiliation from Responsible Broker A to Responsible Broker B. Under W.S. 33-28-109(c), before she may begin acting under Broker B, she must:
choice_a: Notify the commission promptly in writing of the facts attendant to the change, pay the required fee, and be issued a new license under the new responsible broker
choice_b: Wait 30 days after leaving Broker A automatically
choice_c: File the change only with the Wyoming Secretary of State
choice_d: Simply inform Broker A verbally that she is leaving
explanation: 33-28-109(c) requires the licensee to promptly notify the commission in writing, pay the fee, and receive a new license under the new responsible broker before continuing real estate activity. No automatic waiting period or filing with the Secretary of State applies.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Which statement correctly describes the rule on a licensee's affiliation under W.S. 33-28-109(c)?
choice_a: A licensee may associate with two responsible brokers simultaneously if both consent in writing
choice_b: An associate broker or salesperson shall not directly or indirectly associate himself with a responsible broker until he has been issued a license to do so with that broker
choice_c: A licensee may begin working for a new responsible broker immediately upon signing an employment agreement, before any license update
choice_d: Affiliation changes are effective automatically once the prior broker verbally releases the licensee
explanation: 33-28-109(c) provides that no associate broker or salesperson shall directly or indirectly associate with a responsible broker until issued a license to do so with that broker. Simultaneous dual affiliation and self-effectuating verbal releases are not authorized.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-102(a)(xv), a "designated licensee" is defined as:
choice_a: The licensee who physically holds the office key
choice_b: Any licensee with more than five years of experience
choice_c: A licensee designated in writing by a responsible broker to serve as an agent for a seller or buyer, or as an intermediary, in a real estate transaction
choice_d: The licensee approved by the commission chairman for a given transaction
explanation: 33-28-102(b)(xv) defines a "designated licensee" as a licensee designated in writing by a responsible broker to serve as an agent for a seller or buyer or as an intermediary in a transaction. Wyoming uses this mechanism to let different licensees in the same brokerage represent opposing sides.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: For an in-house real estate transaction, W.S. 33-28-302(h) provides that the designated licensee working with a seller or buyer may be:
choice_a: Only a licensed appraiser assigned by the commission
choice_b: Any unlicensed staff member the broker trusts
choice_c: Only the responsible broker personally
choice_d: A responsible broker, an associate broker, or a salesperson under the direct supervision of a responsible broker (who is not a party) or of a transaction manager
explanation: 33-28-302(h) lists who may serve as a designated licensee for an in-house transaction: a responsible broker, an associate broker, a salesperson directly supervised by a responsible broker who is not a party, or a salesperson under a transaction manager's supervision.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Broker Dana's company has designated Salesperson Lee to represent the buyer and Salesperson Kim to represent the seller in the same in-house transaction, and Dana herself is representing one of the parties. Under W.S. 33-28-302(j), Dana must:
choice_a: Immediately appoint a transaction manager, unless the other licensee is an associate broker
choice_b: Terminate one of the two designations to avoid a conflict
choice_c: Personally become an intermediary for both parties
choice_d: Do nothing further, since dual designation alone satisfies the statute
explanation: Under 33-28-302(j), if the responsible broker is representing a buyer or seller in an in-house transaction with another designated licensee, the responsible broker must immediately appoint a transaction manager unless the other licensee is an associate broker.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: When a responsible broker designates two different licensees within the same real estate company to represent the buyer and the seller in the same in-house transaction, W.S. 33-28-302(j) provides that this simultaneous designation:
choice_a: Automatically converts both designated licensees into intermediaries
choice_b: Does not by itself constitute dual agency or require the licensees to act as intermediaries
choice_c: Is void unless both parties are unrepresented customers
choice_d: Requires the responsible broker to withdraw from managing the brokerage for that transaction
explanation: 33-28-302(j) states that simultaneous designations of different licensees for different parties do not constitute dual agency or require the responsible broker or licensee to act as an intermediary unless otherwise required by the article.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A responsible broker is supervising two designated licensees who represent opposing parties in the same in-house transaction. Under W.S. 33-28-302(j), the responsible broker:
choice_a: May review all confidential communications between each designee and their client
choice_b: Must personally negotiate the final price between the parties
choice_c: Has access to information necessary for supervision, but is prohibited from sharing any confidential information of either party learned in the course of supervising
choice_d: Is barred from having any access to transaction information
explanation: 33-28-302(j) gives the responsible broker or transaction manager access to necessary information for supervision but prohibits sharing confidential information of either party learned while supervising the licensees or the transaction.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-308(a), a responsible broker's compensation in a real estate transaction may be paid by:
choice_a: Only the party the broker directly represents
choice_b: Only the seller, regardless of who the broker represents
choice_c: Only a lender involved in financing the transaction
choice_d: The seller, the buyer, a third party, or through sharing or splitting compensation between responsible brokers
explanation: 33-28-308(a) permits a responsible broker's compensation to come from the seller, the buyer, a third party, or through sharing or splitting compensation between responsible brokers.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A responsible broker represents the seller in a transaction, but the buyer also contributes part of the broker's fee. Under W.S. 33-28-308(b), this payment by the buyer:
choice_a: Shall not, by itself, be construed to establish an agency or intermediary relationship between the broker and the buyer
choice_b: Automatically makes the broker the buyer's agent
choice_c: Is prohibited under Wyoming law
choice_d: Automatically converts the transaction to an intermediary relationship for both parties
explanation: 33-28-308(b) provides that payment of compensation shall not be construed to establish an agency or intermediary relationship between the responsible broker and the party who paid it.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Before a buyer's agent may propose to the seller's agent that the buyer's agent be compensated by sharing in compensation paid by the seller, W.S. 33-28-308(e) requires the buyer's agent to first:
choice_a: Notify the commission in writing
choice_b: Obtain the written approval of the buyer
choice_c: Obtain the seller's written consent
choice_d: Wait until after closing to disclose the arrangement
explanation: 33-28-308(e) requires a buyer's agent to obtain the buyer's written approval before proposing to the seller's agent that the buyer's agent share in compensation paid by the seller.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A licensee originally agreed in writing to act as an agent for a buyer, but the parties later consent to the licensee acting instead as an intermediary. Under W.S. 33-28-308(h), the buyer's compensation liability under the new arrangement:
choice_a: Automatically doubles to reflect the added neutrality duties
choice_b: Is eliminated entirely once the licensee becomes an intermediary
choice_c: May not exceed the compensation the buyer would have owed under the initial agency agreement, and any contrary contract provision is void and unenforceable
choice_d: Becomes negotiable only at the commission's discretion
explanation: 33-28-308(h) caps the compensation liability of a party who consents to a change from agent to intermediary at the amount owed under the original agreement, and voids any contract provision to the contrary.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-111(a)(xvii), it is grounds for discipline for an associate broker or salesperson to:
choice_a: Decline to participate in a compensation split with a cooperating brokerage
choice_b: Negotiate compensation terms with a customer
choice_c: Accept compensation only via direct deposit
choice_d: Accept compensation from anyone other than his own responsible broker
explanation: 33-28-111(a)(xvii) makes it grounds for discipline for an associate broker or salesperson to accept compensation from anyone other than his responsible broker. All associate broker/salesperson compensation must flow through the responsible broker.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A responsible broker pays a referral fee to an unlicensed acquaintance for steering a buyer to him. Under W.S. 33-28-110(a) and 33-28-111(a)(xxiii), this conduct is:
choice_a: Unlawful and grounds for discipline, because it is unlawful to compensate an unlicensed person for performing real estate activity
choice_b: Permitted if the fee is under $500
choice_c: Permitted because referral fees are categorically exempt from licensing law
choice_d: Permitted only if the unlicensed person is a Wyoming resident
explanation: 33-28-110(a) makes it unlawful for a responsible broker to compensate anyone who is not a licensee of his company (or another responsible broker) for performing real estate activity, and 33-28-111(a)(xxiii) lists this as grounds for discipline.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Wyoming's mandatory written relationship disclosure under W.S. 33-28-306(a) must, at a minimum, include:
choice_a: The licensee's home mailing address
choice_b: A description of the agency, intermediary, and customer relationships available and a statement that compensation for different relationships is negotiable
choice_c: The exact commission percentage the licensee intends to charge
choice_d: A notarized signature from a commission representative
explanation: 33-28-306(a)(i) requires the written disclosure to describe the different agency, intermediary and customer relationships allowed and to state that compensation for different relationships is negotiable, among other required content.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-309, any written disclosure required under 33-28-306 must be printed in a font size of at least:
choice_a: 10 point
choice_b: 8 point
choice_c: 12 point
choice_d: 14 point
explanation: 33-28-309 requires that any disclosure made under 33-28-306 be in a font size of 12 point or greater.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-306(a), which of the following does NOT, by itself, trigger the requirement to provide a written relationship disclosure?
choice_a: Entering into a written buyer's representation agreement
choice_b: Engaging in a discussion or arrangement incidental to negotiating a purchase of real estate
choice_c: Entering into a written listing agreement with a seller
choice_d: An open house showing or a preliminary conversation involving only a request for factual information
explanation: 33-28-306(a) expressly excludes open house showings, preliminary conversations, and requests for factual information from the definition of discussions or arrangements that trigger the mandatory written disclosure requirement.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A licensee personally owns a fractional interest in a property she is showing to a buyer client but never mentions it. Under W.S. 33-28-111(a)(iii), this is grounds for discipline because:
choice_a: Failing to disclose an interest in the transaction is separately listed as grounds for censure, suspension, or revocation
choice_b: It is only a violation if the licensee also earns a commission on the sale
choice_c: Only sellers, not licensees, have a duty to disclose ownership interests
choice_d: Disclosure of a licensee's ownership interest is required only for commercial property
explanation: 33-28-111(a)(iii) lists "failing to disclose an interest in the transaction" as its own independent ground for commission discipline, regardless of whether a commission is ultimately earned.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A licensee has established an agency relationship with a buyer. Under W.S. 33-28-306(c), the licensee must notify the seller (the other party) of that relationship:
choice_a: Only if the seller specifically asks
choice_b: At the earliest reasonable opportunity
choice_c: Within ten business days after closing
choice_d: At the closing table, and not before
explanation: 33-28-306(c) requires a licensee who has established an agency, subagency, or intermediary relationship with a party to provide notice of that relationship to the other party to the transaction at the earliest reasonable opportunity.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Among a seller's agent's duties under W.S. 33-28-303(a), the agent must present all offers and counteroffers to the seller:
choice_a: Only if the offer meets or exceeds the listing price
choice_b: Only at the seller's specific written request
choice_c: In a timely manner, regardless of whether the property is already subject to a contract for sale
choice_d: Once per week, in a summary report
explanation: 33-28-303(a)(iii)(B) requires a seller's agent to present all offers to and from the seller in a timely manner regardless of whether the property is subject to a contract for sale, though the agent need not solicit additional offers once under contract.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Without the seller's informed consent, W.S. 33-28-303(b) prohibits a seller's agent from disclosing to a buyer:
choice_a: The square footage of the home
choice_b: A known material roof defect
choice_c: The street address of the property
choice_d: That the seller is willing to accept less than the asking price
explanation: 33-28-303(b) bars a seller's agent from disclosing, without the seller's informed consent, that the seller will accept less than the asking price, the seller's motivating factors, or willingness to accept different financing terms. Known material defects must still be disclosed under 303(c).

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-303(c), a seller's agent owes a prospective buyer:
choice_a: No duty or obligation, except to disclose adverse material facts actually known by the licensee, including known title and physical-condition defects
choice_b: The same full fiduciary duties owed to the seller
choice_c: A duty to negotiate directly on the buyer's behalf
choice_d: No duties of any kind, even as to known defects
explanation: 33-28-303(c) provides that a seller's agent owes no duty or obligation to the buyer except to disclose adverse material facts actually known by the licensee, such as known title or physical-condition defects and environmental hazards required by law to be disclosed.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Among a buyer's agent's duties listed in W.S. 33-28-304(a), the agent must inform the buyer that:
choice_a: The buyer is never liable for the agent's conduct under any circumstance
choice_b: The buyer may be vicariously liable for the buyer's agent's acts that the buyer approved, directed, or ratified
choice_c: The buyer's agent bears sole personal liability for any transactional breach
choice_d: The buyer must personally attend the closing to avoid liability
explanation: 33-28-304(a)(iii)(G) requires a buyer's agent to inform the buyer that the buyer may be vicariously liable for the acts of the buyer's agent that the buyer approved, directed, or ratified.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-305(a), a licensee engaged as an intermediary in a Wyoming transaction:
choice_a: Acts as agent for whichever party ultimately pays compensation
choice_b: Owes full fiduciary duty to both parties simultaneously, as a form of dual agency
choice_c: Shall not act as an advocate or agent for either party, and is limited to the specific duties set out in the statute
choice_d: May only be engaged to work with a seller, never a buyer
explanation: 33-28-305(a) provides that an intermediary shall not act as an advocate or agent for either party and is limited to providing the specific services described in 305(b)(ii). Wyoming law separately bars dual agency outright under 302(o).

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Before an intermediary may assist both the buyer and seller in the same real estate transaction, W.S. 33-28-305(b)(ii)(E) requires the intermediary to first:
choice_a: Notify the commission in writing
choice_b: Obtain oral consent only, since intermediary status implies neutrality
choice_c: Do nothing further; consent is presumed once a listing exists
choice_d: Obtain the written consent of the parties
explanation: 33-28-305(b)(ii)(E) requires an intermediary to obtain the written consent of the parties before assisting the buyer and seller in the same transaction.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Wyoming's required intermediary disclosure under W.S. 33-28-305(b)(ii)(K) specifically informs the parties that an intermediary:
choice_a: Owes no fiduciary duty to either party, may not negotiate on behalf of either party, and may be required to disclose information learned about the property to the other side
choice_b: Owes full fiduciary duty to whichever party makes the request
choice_c: Is prohibited from disclosing any information to either party under any circumstance
choice_d: May negotiate exclusively on the seller's behalf once engaged
explanation: 33-28-305(b)(ii)(K) requires disclosure that the intermediary owes no fiduciary duty to either buyer or seller, is not allowed to negotiate on behalf of either, and may be required to disclose information learned about the property to the other party.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-302(p), absent a written agency or intermediary agreement, the default relationship between a licensee and a party to a transaction is that of:
choice_a: An implied single agency
choice_b: A customer, to whom the licensee owes no duty of confidentiality
choice_c: An implied intermediary relationship
choice_d: A subagent of the listing broker
explanation: 33-28-302(p) provides that a customer relationship exists between a licensee and any party unless a single agency or intermediary relationship is established through a written agreement, and that a licensee owes no duty of confidentiality to a customer.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-311, in a property management or leasing context, a licensee working with a landlord under a written agreement is presumed to be working with the tenant as:
choice_a: The tenant's automatic agent
choice_b: An automatic intermediary
choice_c: A customer, unless the parties have agreed otherwise in writing
choice_d: A subagent of the tenant
explanation: 33-28-311(a) provides that a licensee is deemed to work with the landlord as agent or intermediary under a written agreement, and with the tenant as a customer unless otherwise provided for in writing between the parties.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A licensee unreasonably refuses, upon demand, to surrender to the rightful owner a document in her possession related to a closed transaction. Under W.S. 33-28-111(a)(xi), this is:
choice_a: Permissible if the document is kept in a locked file cabinet
choice_b: A violation only if the document is an original recorded deed
choice_c: A violation only if a court order first compels release
choice_d: Grounds for censure, suspension, or revocation of her license
explanation: 33-28-111(a)(xi) makes it grounds for discipline to unreasonably fail, upon demand, to surrender to the rightful owner any document or instrument in the licensee's possession.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: During a commission investigation into a transaction, a licensee unreasonably refuses to produce transaction records in his possession. This is grounds for discipline under:
choice_a: 33-28-111(a)(xii), which makes unreasonably failing to produce records under commission investigation a separate violation
choice_b: 33-28-122, the trust account statute, exclusively
choice_c: No statute; record production during an investigation is voluntary
choice_d: 33-28-118, the license renewal statute
explanation: 33-28-111(a)(xii) lists unreasonably failing to produce documents of record in a licensee's possession or control concerning a transaction under commission investigation as independent grounds for discipline.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Which of the following is listed as grounds for discipline under W.S. 33-28-111(a)(xxi)?
choice_a: Delivering a signed contract electronically rather than on paper
choice_b: Failing to deliver, within a reasonable time, a completed copy of any document to all parties
choice_c: Retaining a digital copy of a fully executed contract
choice_d: Delivering a signed listing agreement one business day after signature
explanation: 33-28-111(a)(xxi) makes it grounds for discipline to fail to deliver a completed copy of any document to all parties within a reasonable time. Electronic delivery or a one-day turnaround, standing alone, is not a violation.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-123, a responsible broker must retain a full set of records of a real estate transaction in which he participated for at least:
choice_a: Six months from the date of closing
choice_b: One year from the date of closing
choice_c: Two years from the latest date on which the real estate company participated in the transaction
choice_d: Five years from the date the file was opened
explanation: 33-28-123 requires records of every transaction to be maintained for not less than two years from the latest date on which the real estate company participated in the transaction.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-122(a)(i) and 33-28-111(a)(xxvii), earnest money and other trust funds received by a responsible broker or his licensees must be deposited in a trust or escrow account:
choice_a: Within thirty calendar days of receipt
choice_b: Within one banking day, with no exceptions ever permitted
choice_c: By the last business day of the calendar month
choice_d: Within one banking day, unless all persons having an interest in the funds have agreed otherwise in writing
explanation: 33-28-122(a)(i) and 33-28-111(a)(xxvii) require trust funds to be deposited within one banking day, unless every person with an interest in the funds has agreed otherwise in writing.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A Wyoming trust account is interest-bearing, and the parties never signed a written agreement about how interest should be distributed. Under W.S. 33-28-122(c), accrued interest on withdrawn funds must be:
choice_a: Paid out to the person(s) from whom the trust funds were received, in proportion to the funds withdrawn and paid out to each
choice_b: Retained by the responsible broker as administrative compensation
choice_c: Donated to the Wyoming real estate recovery account
choice_d: Split evenly between the buyer and seller regardless of who deposited the funds
explanation: 33-28-122(c) provides that, absent a written agreement, interest accrued on withdrawn trust funds must be paid to the person(s) from whom the funds were received, proportionate to what each is entitled to receive.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A licensee is holding earnest money that she expects will ultimately be applied toward her commission. Under W.S. 33-28-122(d), she is entitled to treat those funds as her own compensation:
choice_a: Immediately upon receiving the earnest money
choice_b: Only once the transaction has been consummated or terminated
choice_c: As soon as the purchase contract is fully signed by both parties
choice_d: Once the buyer has been pre-approved for financing
explanation: 33-28-122(d) provides that a licensee is not entitled to any part of the earnest money or other item of value as part of his compensation until the transaction has been consummated or terminated.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A responsible broker deposits a small amount of his own money into the trust account solely to keep the account open and avoid a minimum-balance fee. Under W.S. 33-28-122(e), this deposit:
choice_a: Is always prohibited commingling of personal and trust funds
choice_b: Is permitted only with the commission's prior written approval
choice_c: Is not considered commingling, provided the deposit is identified at the time it is made
choice_d: Is permitted only if withdrawn again within 24 hours
explanation: 33-28-122(e) states it will not be considered commingling if, when establishing the trust account, the broker deposits some of his own funds to keep the account open or avoid minimum-balance charges, so long as that deposit is identified at the time of deposit.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A buyer and seller dispute whether an earnest money deposit should be returned or forfeited. Under W.S. 33-28-122(f), the responsible broker holding the deposit must:
choice_a: Immediately release the funds to the seller, since the seller is the principal
choice_b: Immediately release the funds to the buyer to avoid liability
choice_c: Split the disputed funds evenly between the parties pending resolution
choice_d: Continue holding the funds in trust until receiving a written release from the parties, until a civil action is filed, or until he interpleads the funds with the court
explanation: 33-28-122(f) requires the broker to continue holding a disputed deposit in trust until a written release is signed by the parties, a civil action is filed, or the broker interpleads all parties and pays the funds to the court.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-111(a)(xx), a licensee's failure to obtain a written listing agreement identifying the property and containing which of the following is grounds for discipline?
choice_a: The price or price range, the compensation to be paid, the signatures of all parties concerned, and a definite expiration date
choice_b: Only the seller's signature, nothing more
choice_c: Only the asking price of the property
choice_d: Only the amount of compensation to be paid
explanation: 33-28-111(a)(xx) requires written listing agreements identifying the property and containing all terms, including price or price range, compensation, signatures of all parties, and a definite expiration date.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-111(a)(vii), placing a "for sale" or "for rent" sign on a property is grounds for discipline unless the licensee first obtains:
choice_a: Approval from the local homeowners' association
choice_b: The written consent of the owner or the owner's authorized agent
choice_c: A permit from the county planning office
choice_d: Verbal permission, which is sufficient in all cases
explanation: 33-28-111(a)(vii) makes it grounds for discipline to place a sign on any property offering it for sale or rent without the written consent of the owner or his authorized agent.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A licensee advertises a property for lease on terms the owner never authorized. Under W.S. 33-28-111(a)(viii), this violates Wyoming law's prohibition on:
choice_a: Using interior photographs without the owner's separate consent
choice_b: Advertising rental property without a separate property management license
choice_c: Offering real estate for sale or lease without the owner's knowledge and consent, or on terms other than those the owner authorized
choice_d: Listing property below its assessed tax value
explanation: 33-28-111(a)(viii) prohibits offering real estate for sale or lease without the knowledge and consent of the owner or authorized agent, or on terms other than those the owner authorized.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A licensee contacts a seller who is currently under an exclusive listing agreement with another responsible broker and urges the seller to cancel that listing and sign with the licensee instead. Under W.S. 33-28-111(a)(iv), this is grounds for discipline as:
choice_a: Permissible competitive prospecting, since no contract has actually been breached yet
choice_b: A violation only if compensation ultimately changes hands
choice_c: A violation only if the seller actually cancels the existing listing
choice_d: Soliciting the breach of a listing or property management contract
explanation: 33-28-111(a)(iv) lists soliciting the breach of a listing or property management contract as grounds for discipline; the violation occurs at the solicitation, not only upon an actual breach.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-302(q), the proprietary ownership interest in a written listing agreement obtained by a salesperson while working for her company is vested in:
choice_a: The responsible broker
choice_b: The seller who signed the listing
choice_c: The salesperson personally
choice_d: The Wyoming Real Estate Commission
explanation: 33-28-302(q) provides that the proprietary ownership interest of written listing agreements is vested in the responsible broker, not in the individual salesperson who took the listing.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Since January 1, 2008, W.S. 33-28-401(a) has required Wyoming licensees applying for, renewing, or reactivating a license to:
choice_a: Carry general commercial liability insurance instead of errors and omissions coverage
choice_b: Submit proof of errors and omissions insurance coverage through the group program or certified individual coverage
choice_c: Obtain errors and omissions insurance only if the licensee personally handles trust funds
choice_d: Obtain errors and omissions coverage only during the licensee's first year of practice
explanation: 33-28-401(a) requires an applicant, a licensee renewing a license, or an inactive licensee activating a license to submit proof of E&O coverage through the commission's group program or through certification of individual coverage.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Regarding the group errors and omissions insurance program, W.S. 33-28-401(b) requires that any group program the commission obtains through competitive bidding:
choice_a: Be optional and available only to responsible brokers, not associate brokers or salespersons
choice_b: Allow the insurer discretion to cancel high-risk licensees
choice_c: Be available to all licensees and prevent the insurer from canceling coverage on any individual licensee
choice_d: Be re-bid every single year with no multi-year contracts permitted
explanation: 33-28-401(b) requires that the group program be available to all licensees and prevent the insurer from canceling any licensee's coverage.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-401(d), if the commission is unable to obtain group errors and omissions coverage at a reasonable annual premium not exceeding the statutory cap (adjusted annually for inflation), the E&O insurance requirement for that year:
choice_a: Is permanently waived for all future license periods
choice_b: Shifts automatically to a mandatory individual policy at licensee expense, with no cap
choice_c: Triggers a special assessment against all licensees to fund coverage
choice_d: Does not apply, with the statutory premium cap beginning at $300.00 per licensee
explanation: 33-28-401(d) provides that if the commission cannot obtain group coverage at a reasonable annual premium not exceeding $300.00 per licensee (adjusted annually for inflation), the E&O requirement does not apply for that year.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-401(e), the administrative fee the commission may charge licensees who participate in the group E&O program, in addition to the insurance premium, is capped at:
choice_a: Ten percent of the premium
choice_b: A flat $50 regardless of the premium amount
choice_c: Twenty-five percent of the premium
choice_d: There is no statutory cap on the administrative fee
explanation: 33-28-401(e) authorizes the commission to charge an administrative fee, in an amount sufficient to cover administration, that shall not exceed ten percent of the premium.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-401(c), the commission must notify each licensee of the required errors and omissions insurance terms and conditions how long before the license renewal date?
choice_a: Ten days
choice_b: At least thirty days
choice_c: Five days
choice_d: Sixty days
explanation: 33-28-401(c) requires the commission to notify each licensee of the required E&O terms and conditions at least thirty days prior to the license renewal date.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-111(a), the Wyoming Real Estate Commission may impose an administrative fine for each separate offense not to exceed:
explanation: 33-28-111(a) authorizes the commission to impose an administrative fine not to exceed $2,500.00 for each separate offense, in addition to censure, probation, suspension, or revocation.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A licensee tells a buyer in writing that a property is "guaranteed to double in value within five years" in order to close the sale. This is prohibited because W.S. 33-28-111(a)(xix):
choice_a: Only prohibits sellers, not licensees, from making such statements
choice_b: Permits such statements only if later proven true
choice_c: Only prohibits such guarantees if made orally, not in writing
choice_d: Forbids guaranteeing, or authorizing any person to guarantee, future profits which may result from the resale of real estate
explanation: 33-28-111(a)(xix) makes it grounds for discipline for a licensee to guarantee, or authorize anyone to guarantee, future profits from the resale of real estate, regardless of whether the guarantee is later borne out.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: A buyer wants to submit a promissory note instead of cash as earnest money. Under W.S. 33-28-111(a)(xxxi), the licensee may accept it only if:
choice_a: This is communicated to the owner prior to the owner's acceptance of the offer, and the fact is shown in the earnest money receipt
choice_b: The Wyoming Real Estate Commission pre-approves the substitution
choice_c: The listing broker personally co-signs the promissory note
choice_d: The buyer's agent independently guarantees the note's value
explanation: 33-28-111(a)(xxxi) permits accepting other than cash as earnest money only if the fact is communicated to the owner before acceptance of the offer to purchase and is shown in the earnest money receipt.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Which conviction is expressly listed in W.S. 33-28-111(a)(xxii) as grounds for suspension or revocation of a Wyoming real estate license?
choice_a: Any misdemeanor traffic violation
choice_b: A felony that relates to the practice of real estate activity or to the ability to perform the duties of a licensee, or any felony sexual offense or violent crime
choice_c: A civil judgment arising from an unrelated contract dispute
choice_d: A speeding ticket received while showing property
explanation: 33-28-111(a)(xxii) lists conviction of a felony related to real estate practice or the ability to perform licensee duties, or any felony sexual offense or violent crime, as grounds for suspension or revocation.

topic: Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees
question: Under W.S. 33-28-111(a)(xxxiii), receiving more than how many censures from the commission within a two-year period is itself separately listed as grounds for discipline?
choice_a: More than ten
choice_b: More than one
choice_c: More than three
choice_d: More than five
explanation: 33-28-111(a)(xxxiii) lists receiving more than three censures from the commission within a two-year period as its own separate ground for discipline.
